title: Tipoff catalog
description: Single versioned data file: points programs, cards, merchant chains with pre-seeded MCCs, and MCC/POI category mappings. Documentation + external tooling contract. The app gates acceptance with CatalogValidator (Swift), which enforces every constraint declared here (bounds, patterns, lengths, arity) plus cross-references (program IDs exist, chain MCCs are mapped, poolsWith IDs exist, >=100 cards, >=100 chains). Forward compatibility: an entry whose rewardCategory this build does not know is dropped at decode with a warning (never remapped); an unknown earnRate.channel decodes as any with a warning.

catalogVersion.description: YYYY.MM.DD-N. Bump N for same-day re-releases.

mccToCategory.description: Four-digit MCC -> reward category, optionally with a confidence (default 0.9) that caps any chain match whose mcc is this code (after the POI bonus) — e.g. 5499 convenience stores are groceries at 0.45 because issuers disagree. Two bands only (PLAN §16.8.2): < 0.5 display-only, >= 0.5 push-eligible. Every MCC referenced by a chain must be present. Codes in 3000-3299, 3351-3441 and 3501-3999 fall back to travel at runtime when absent.

poiToCategory.description: MKPointOfInterestCategory short name (rawValue without the MKPOICategory prefix, lowerCamel; acronyms lowercased: evCharger, atm, rvPark) -> [category, confidence 0..1]. Keys are compared case-insensitively at runtime and must not collide by case. Every key must be a real MKPointOfInterestCategory.

poiCorroboration.description: PLAN §16.24.1: reward category (raw value, e.g. "dining") -> extra keywords whose presence in the place name, beyond the matched chain alias, corroborates a disagreeing POI's classification of that category. "Kroger Cafe" corroborates a restaurant POI's dining category via "cafe"; a bare "Kroger" does not, so the chain result stays display-only at 0.45 instead of pushing dining. A category with no entry here (e.g. groceries) can never be corroborated by name alone. Optional — absent on an older cached catalog behaves as an empty table (every disagreement stays display-only). An unrecognized key is ignored by CategoryMapper and flagged by the validator, never fatal.

rate.description: Multiplier (points programs) or percent (cash programs). 0 is legal but the validator warns.

rewardCategory.description: Phase 1 live: dining, groceries, gas, travel, everythingElse. Reserved: transit, streaming, drugstores, onlineRetail, wholesaleClubs. An unknown string drops the containing row/entry at decode with a warning (forward compatibility).

defaultCentsPerPoint.description: Editorial default valuation. 1.0 for cash. Users override per program.

kind.description: points: card rates are multipliers (4x). cash: card rates are percents (3%).

cap.description: Phase 2 schema. Ignored by the Phase 1 engine.

capGroupID.description: PLAN §17.8.1 shared cap: rows on ONE card that carry the same capGroupID draw from a single bucket (Citi Custom Cash's $500/month top-category pot, BofA Customized Cash's $2,500/quarter choice pot, Marriott Boundless's $6,000/year across dining, gas and groceries). Every row in a group must repeat the same cap, capPeriod and capUnit (validator error card.earn.capGroup.disagreement), and a grouped row must declare a cap. Absent = the row's cap is its own, per category, as PLAN §17.2 shipped. The id is scoped to the card; two cards may reuse the same string.

channel.description: Where the row applies. Absent = any. Location alerts, the widget and the manual picker score only any + inStore; Card Detail shows online/portal rows with a label ("online only", "via Chase Travel"). One row per (category, channel, chainIDs restriction); everythingElse rows are exempt from that rule and only warn unless merchant-restricted. An unknown value decodes as any with a warning.

chainIDs.description: PLAN §16.10 / §16.13.3 merchant-restricted row: applies ONLY when the resolved chain (or its fuelSiblingID parent) is listed (Hilton Aspire 14x at hilton, Delta Gold 2x at delta_air_lines, Costco Anywhere 5% at costco_fuel and 2% at costco, Target Circle 5% at target). Every id must exist in chains[] (warning otherwise) and at least one listed chain — or its fuel sibling — must classify as the row's category, or the row can never apply (validator warning card.earn.chainIDs.category; build.py asserts). Manual mode (no chain context) ignores restricted rows. A restricted everythingElse row is the only legal everythingElse row and, per PLAN §16.13.1, is push-eligible ("Use Target Circle MC · 5% here").

excludedChainIDs.description: PLAN §16.11.2 merchant exclusion: the row does NOT apply at these chains (Amex/Chase/Capital One/BofA grocery rows exclude walmart, target); the card falls to its next applicable row / flatRate there. Every id must exist in chains[]. Manual mode ignores exclusions.

program.description: Rotating program identifier, e.g. chase_freedom_flex, discover_it.

rate.description: Scored as the card's rate for a category the current quarter covers (PLAN §16.31.1), and rendered as a percent in the unannounced-quarter hedge.

cap.description: PLAN §16.31.3: dollars of spend the bonus rate covers per quarter (1500 on both seeded programs). Disclosed in copy; not enforced.

calendar.description: The announced quarters (PLAN §16.28 A). A quarter that covers the requested category is scored at `rate` (PLAN §16.31.1).

activationApp.description: USER-FACING, and optional on purpose (PLAN §28.1). The app a cardholder activates this quarter's categories in, interpolated into the activation prompt. Omit it when the destination is not knowable for every holder of the card: Discover accounts are migrating to Capital One in waves through early 2027, so a Discover card naming either app would be wrong for some readers, and the copy falls back to "Activate this quarter".

benefit.description: PLAN §17.4.1 / §17.7 — a statement credit or recurring perk. cadence, resetRule and channel are loose strings so a value a future catalog introduces never breaks decoding (§16.22.5); an unrecognised cadence or resetRule decodes with a warning and the tracker derives no window from it.

cadence.description: The human label. The window itself comes from resetRule, or from intervalMonths when present.

resetRule.description: Which window the allowance belongs to. PLAN §17.7.1 added calendarHalf (Jan–Jun / Jul–Dec) because deriving two windows from semiannual + calendarYear would be guesswork at the boundary. cardmemberYear runs from the user's own anniversary, which the data does not carry — the tracker treats it as calendarYear and says so on screen (§17.9). §17.10.5 added "interval", which pairs with intervalMonths: set them together or the validator warns.

intervalMonths.description: PLAN §17.7.2 — months between renewals for a credit no cadence expresses (48 for Global Entry / TSA PreCheck). When present it drives the reset, measured from the user's last recorded use, and cadence/resetRule are the label only.

geofenceable.description: PLAN §17.7.3 — whether arriving somewhere can ever be the moment to use this credit. false for a delivery or booking platform (DoorDash, Instacart, Resy, Uber): there is no arrival, and Resy's credit applies at partner restaurants the catalog cannot name. Absent = true. The arrival path may only ever offer a geofenceable credit; the Benefits tab shows every credit either way. A credit marked true whose chains are all platform entries is a validator error (card.benefit.geofenceable.platform). PLAN §17.10.2: channel portalCredit implies false, and a portalCredit marked true is a validator error (card.benefit.geofenceable.portal) — a portal credit is redeemed by booking, so no arrival is the moment to spend it. §17.10.3: the Turo credit is marked false directly rather than reclassifying the turo chain.

chainIDs.description: PLAN §17.4.1 — the merchants the credit is spent at, so the arrival path can offer it ("you have $8 of Dunkin credit"). Every id must exist in chains[] (validator warning otherwise; build.py asserts the bundled data).

enrollmentRequired.description: PLAN §17.10.4 — whether the cardholder must opt in before a dollar of this credit is spendable (Resy, the Instacart and DoorDash promos, Amex's enrolment offers). Absent = false. An enrollment-gated credit the user has not confirmed enrolling in is not available money: the Benefits tab shows an "enroll first" state, never counts it toward a balance, and never offers it on arrival.

verifiedAt.description: Editorial sign-off date, as on card.verifiedAt (PLAN §16.12.5). null/absent = unverified.

note.description: Editorial note: what the amount covers, what it excludes, where it was confirmed.

editorialNote.description: NOT user-facing. Where provenance for this credit belongs (PLAN §26.1): a PLAN reference, a run name or a dated correction. `note` above is rendered verbatim to the cardholder and must carry none of that, so this field is what keeps the two apart. No screen reads this one.

earn.description: May be empty (pure flat card). One row per (category, channel, chainIDs restriction). Co-brand cards (PLAN §16.13.3): the brand rate is a chainIDs row; the unrestricted travel row, if any, is the 'other travel' rate.

verifiedAt.description: Editorial sign-off date (PLAN §16.12.5): the date every modelled field was checked against sourceURL (2026-09-06 for the first pass). null = seeded from general knowledge, unverified, or pending founder confirmation (a PENDING_CONFIRMATION comment in the generator). Re-verify quarterly.

status.description: PLAN §16.12.2 lifecycle. active: open to new applicants. closedToNew: existing holders keep it; the picker lists it with the caption "No longer offered to new applicants" (Citi Custom Cash, legacy Bilt). converted: every account was migrated to convertedTo; hidden from the picker; holders see a one-time "Your <old> is now <new>" notice with Replace/Keep. discontinued: retired; hidden from the picker; kept so saved states resolve. An unknown value decodes as active with a warning.

convertedTo.description: For status=converted: the successor card id (must exist in cards[] and not be this card — validator error otherwise; a non-converted card with convertedTo, or a converted card without it, warns).

notes.description: PLAN §23.1 — USER-FACING. Card Detail renders it verbatim: plain language about how the card earns, for someone deciding which card to pull out. A PLAN reference, a run name (M12a, Run 20), a section sign or the word "ruling" is a validator error; that text belongs in editorialNotes.

editorialNotes.description: PLAN §23.1 — editorial provenance: rulings, sources, caveats and do-not-re-add warnings. Never rendered on any screen. A note that mixes both is split sentence by sentence rather than filed whole in one field.

standaloneCentsPerPoint.description: Points pooling (PLAN §16.3.2): value of a point when the user owns none of poolsWith (e.g. Freedom 1.0). Absent = always the program default. Requires poolsWith.

poolsWith.description: Card IDs (must exist in cards[] and share programID) that lift this card's points to the program default when owned. Requires standaloneCentsPerPoint.

displayRatesAsPercent.description: PLAN §16.6.2: a points-modelled card the issuer markets in percent (Citi Double Cash, Custom Cash, Rewards+). displayRate renders rate × standaloneCentsPerPoint as a percent ("2%", "5%"); displayReturn still uses the effective (pooled or standalone) valuation.

brandNames.description: Matched case-insensitively after normalization. A multi-word alias (contains whitespace) matches anywhere as a contiguous whole-token sequence at 0.9 confidence; a single-word alias matches only at the START of the place name at 0.75. Longest alias wins. Never list a bare common word (United, Lucky, Pilot, Apple).

nameRegex.description: Optional ICU regex (case-insensitive) applied to the raw name; checked before aliases at 0.9. PLAN §16.8.1: only patterns whose exact string is compiled into the app (ChainRegexWhitelist.swift) are ever run; any other pattern — from a remote catalog or a typo here — is dropped with a validator warning and the chain falls back to alias matching. Only run against names of at most 128 characters.

mcc.description: Should be a key of mccToCategory (the validator warns otherwise — PLAN §16.8.9; the chain's own category is authoritative). That entry's confidence caps the chain's match confidence, after the POI bonus.

confidence.description: seeded: match-kind confidence applies. confirmed: 0.97. disputed: 0.5.

acceptedNetworks.description: Card networks accepted at this chain (PLAN §16.2.2). Absent = all. Costco / Costco fuel are ["visa"]; the engine excludes other cards and reports them in Recommendation.excludedForNetwork.

active.description: false keeps a retired chain (rite_aid) for history; inactive chains never match.

platform.description: PLAN §17.7.3/§17.7.4 — a delivery or booking platform (resy, instacart, doordash), not a place a user arrives at. A platform entry exists so a benefit can name where its credit is spent; it is never matched against a place name, so it produces no classification and no arrival, and a benefit naming only platforms must set geofenceable: false.

fuelSiblingID.description: PLAN §16.8.7: the 5541 chain a gasStation POI at this chain resolves to, at 0.85 (costco → costco_fuel, kroger → kroger_fuel). Must exist in chains[] and be a gas chain.
